Apply \(C_2 \to C_2 + C_3\). Every entry of the new \(C_2\) becomes \(a+b+c\):
\(\begin{vmatrix}1 & a+b+c & b+c\\ 1 & a+b+c & c+a\\ 1 & a+b+c & a+b\end{vmatrix}\)
Take the common factor \(a+b+c\) out of \(C_2\):
\(= (a+b+c)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & b+c\\ 1 & 1 & c+a\\ 1 & 1 & a+b\end{vmatrix}\)
Here \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are identical, and a determinant with two identical columns is zero.
Value of the determinant \(= 0\)

Every entry of \(R_3\) carries the factor \(3x\), since \(6x = 3x(2)\), \(9x = 3x(3)\), \(12x = 3x(4)\). Taking \(3x\) out of \(R_3\):
\(\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 & 4\\ 5 & 6 & 8\\ 6x & 9x & 12x\end{vmatrix} = 3x\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 & 4\\ 5 & 6 & 8\\ 2 & 3 & 4\end{vmatrix}\)
Now \(R_1\) and \(R_3\) are identical, so the determinant is zero.
Value of the determinant \(= 0\)

Observe that the third column is built from the first two: \(65 = 2 + 9(7)\), \(75 = 3 + 9(8)\), \(86 = 5 + 9(9)\), i.e. \(C_3 = C_1 + 9C_2\).
Apply \(C_3 \to C_3 - C_1 - 9C_2\):
\(\begin{vmatrix}2 & 7 & 65\\ 3 & 8 & 75\\ 5 & 9 & 86\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 7 & 0\\ 3 & 8 & 0\\ 5 & 9 & 0\end{vmatrix}\)
Every entry of \(C_3\) is now zero, and a determinant with a zero column is zero.
Value of the determinant \(= 0\)

Let \(s = x+y+z\) and let \(L\) be the determinant on the left.
Apply \(R_1 \to R_1 + R_2 + R_3\). Each entry of the new \(R_1\) is \((x+y)+(z+x)+(y+z) = 2s\), so taking \(2s\) out of \(R_1\):
\(L = 2s\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\ z+x & x+y & y+z\\ y+z & z+x & x+y\end{vmatrix}\)
Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 + R_3\); the new \(R_2\) is \((s+z,\ s+x,\ s+y)\). Now apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - sR_1\), which makes \(R_2 = (z,\ x,\ y)\). Finally apply \(R_3 \to R_3 - R_2\), which makes \(R_3 = (y+z-z,\ z+x-x,\ x+y-y) = (y,\ z,\ x)\). Hence
\(L = 2s\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\ z & x & y\\ y & z & x\end{vmatrix}\)
Now treat the right-hand side. In \(\begin{vmatrix}x & y & z\\ z & x & y\\ y & z & x\end{vmatrix}\) apply \(R_1 \to R_1 + R_2 + R_3\); each entry of the new \(R_1\) is \(s\), so taking \(s\) out of \(R_1\):
\(2\begin{vmatrix}x & y & z\\ z & x & y\\ y & z & x\end{vmatrix} = 2s\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\ z & x & y\\ y & z & x\end{vmatrix}\)
The two sides have been reduced to the same expression.
\(\therefore \begin{vmatrix}x+y & y+z & z+x\\ z+x & x+y & y+z\\ y+z & z+x & x+y\end{vmatrix} = 2\begin{vmatrix}x & y & z\\ z & x & y\\ y & z & x\end{vmatrix}\)

Let \(D = \begin{vmatrix}a+b & a & b\\ a & a+c & c\\ b & c & b+c\end{vmatrix}\).
Apply \(R_1 \to R_1 - R_2 - R_3\). The new \(R_1\) is \(\big((a+b)-a-b,\ a-(a+c)-c,\ b-c-(b+c)\big) = (0,\ -2c,\ -2c)\). Taking \(-2c\) out of \(R_1\):
\(D = -2c\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 1\\ a & a+c & c\\ b & c & b+c\end{vmatrix}\)
Apply \(C_3 \to C_3 - C_2\):
\(D = -2c\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 0\\ a & a+c & -a\\ b & c & b\end{vmatrix}\)
Expanding along \(R_1\), only the entry \(1\) survives:
\(D = -2c\left[-1\begin{vmatrix}a & -a\\ b & b\end{vmatrix}\right] = -2c\big[-(ab + ab)\big] = -2c(-2ab)\)
\(\therefore D = 4abc\)

Here \(x,\ y,\ z\) are positive and none of them is \(1\). Write every logarithm in one common base using \(\log_p q = \frac{\log q}{\log p}\):
\(\begin{vmatrix}1 & \log_x y & \log_x z\\ \log_y x & 1 & \log_y z\\ \log_z x & \log_z y & 1\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}\frac{\log x}{\log x} & \frac{\log y}{\log x} & \frac{\log z}{\log x}\\ \frac{\log x}{\log y} & \frac{\log y}{\log y} & \frac{\log z}{\log y}\\ \frac{\log x}{\log z} & \frac{\log y}{\log z} & \frac{\log z}{\log z}\end{vmatrix}\)
Take \(\frac{1}{\log x}\) out of \(R_1\), \(\frac{1}{\log y}\) out of \(R_2\) and \(\frac{1}{\log z}\) out of \(R_3\):
\(= \frac{1}{\log x \cdot \log y \cdot \log z}\begin{vmatrix}\log x & \log y & \log z\\ \log x & \log y & \log z\\ \log x & \log y & \log z\end{vmatrix}\)
All three rows are identical, so this determinant is zero.
\(\therefore \begin{vmatrix}1 & \log_x y & \log_x z\\ \log_y x & 1 & \log_y z\\ \log_z x & \log_z y & 1\end{vmatrix} = 0\)

Every entry below the main diagonal is \(0\), so the determinant is upper triangular and its value is the product of the diagonal entries:
\((x-1)(x-2)(x-3) = 0\)
Hence \(x - 1 = 0\) or \(x - 2 = 0\) or \(x - 3 = 0\).
\(x = 1\) or \(x = 2\) or \(x = 3\)

Apply \(R_1 \to R_1 + R_2 + R_3\). Each entry of the new \(R_1\) is \((4+x)+(4-x)+(4-x) = 12-x\), so taking \(12-x\) out of \(R_1\):
\((12-x)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\ 4-x & 4+x & 4-x\\ 4-x & 4-x & 4+x\end{vmatrix} = 0\)
Apply \(C_2 \to C_2 - C_1\) and \(C_3 \to C_3 - C_1\):
\((12-x)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\ 4-x & 2x & 0\\ 4-x & 0 & 2x\end{vmatrix} = 0\)
Expanding along \(R_1\): \((12-x)(2x)(2x) = 0\), i.e. \(4x^2(12-x) = 0\).
\(x = 0\) or \(x = 12\)

Let \(D = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 1\\ 3 & 1 & 7\\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{vmatrix}\) (the determinant on the right) and let \(G = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\ 3 & 1 & 7\\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{vmatrix}\). Use the fact that a determinant is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged, and that a determinant is a sum when one row is written as a sum.
Second determinant on the left: interchanging rows and columns,
\(\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 & 3\\ 2 & 1 & 2\\ 1 & 7 & 6\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 & 1\\ 3 & 1 & 7\\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{vmatrix}\)
Its first row is \((2,\ 2,\ 1) = (1,\ 2,\ 1) + (1,\ 0,\ 0)\), so splitting the first row gives \(D + G\).
First determinant on the left: interchanging rows and columns,
\(\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 & 6\\ 6 & 1 & 4\\ 3 & 7 & 12\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 6 & 3\\ 3 & 1 & 7\\ 6 & 4 & 12\end{vmatrix}\)
Here \(R_3 = 2(3,\ 2,\ 6)\); taking \(2\) out of \(R_3\) gives \(2\begin{vmatrix}1 & 6 & 3\\ 3 & 1 & 7\\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{vmatrix}\). Its first row is \((1,\ 6,\ 3) = 3(1,\ 2,\ 1) - 2(1,\ 0,\ 0)\), so splitting the first row gives \(2(3D - 2G) = 6D - 4G\).
Adding the two parts of the left-hand side,
\((6D - 4G) + 4(D + G) = 10D\)
\(\therefore \begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 & 6\\ 6 & 1 & 4\\ 3 & 7 & 12\end{vmatrix} + 4\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 & 3\\ 2 & 1 & 2\\ 1 & 7 & 6\end{vmatrix} = 10\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 1\\ 3 & 1 & 7\\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{vmatrix}\)
